pole_plus.label: Row-ending line breaks (newline / backslash-newline) deep inside long raw hex/byte-data dumps (\xNN/octal/\u escape strings, hash and byte lists), ramping with dump length; separate offshoots: Python ', '.join separator, long 'ha ha' runs, plus a diffuse low-precision tail of prose/code tokens

pole_minus.label: Token inside or right after a structured numeric/code value: unit after a dimension (9x13 inch), nested-array row closer '],' (even with word items), deep characters of long alphanumeric IDs/hex strings, delimiters after phone numbers and citation years

rejected_labels: + sentence-final period ending a factual sentence (H+2 0/8; corpus top examples are window-start artifacts, 0.95->0.16 after preamble)
+ sentence boundary / sentence-initial connective (same firing rate sentence-initially and mid-sentence)
+ closing brackets / continuation indentation of multi-line code (H+3 0/8)
+ Python string separator before .join as main label (H+1 2/8; only ', ' fires)
+ any long non-linguistic token run (holdout 2/8 predicted-fire reached 0.3)
+ line breaks in backslash-escape dumps only (R3: 3/8 false positives on hash list, 0x list, no-linebreak dump)
- any digit-bearing number or code (R3 4/8; versions 0.07, coordinates 0.25)
- list delimiters require numeric items (nested word lists fire 0.87 on '],')
- comma-newline continuing multi-line argument lists as a reliable job (R5 3/6)
